cases.summary: Repairs a poor popover transition with bounded motion guidance.
cases.setup: Use a fixture web application with an existing popover primitive, motion tokens, reduced-motion convention, and local browser tooling.
cases.prompt: This popover grows from the center with transition: all 400ms ease-in and scale(0). Make the interaction feel responsive and verify it.
expectedBehavior: Discovers emil-design-eng and routes to apply mode without loading unrelated vocabulary, Apple, or prototype material.
Uses existing project conventions, a trigger-derived origin, named properties, a near-final starting scale, and reduced-motion behavior.
Runs mechanical checks and reports browser or visual checks only when actually performed.
forbiddenBehavior: Applies every house value as a universal law.
Claims compositor, frame-rate, accessibility, or visual success without evidence.
Rebuilds unrelated static styling or UX flow.

cases.summary: Finds restrained motion opportunities and rejects unnecessary animation.
cases.setup: Use a keyboard-heavy settings fixture with one occasional drawer that teleports, several already-clear state changes, and no need for source edits.
cases.prompt: What should animate here to make this feel better without slowing down frequent work?
expectedBehavior: Routes to opportunities mode and remains read-only.
Applies frequency, purpose, budget, function, and evidence gates with file-line citations.
Produces a capped list, representative rejected candidates, and allows most candidates to fail.
forbiddenBehavior: Suggests animation on every inspected control.
Edits source or writes implementation plans.
Treats keyboard-triggered motion or transform-only animation as context-free rules.

cases.summary: Builds distinct interaction-aware UI variants safely on an existing route.
cases.setup: Use a fixture web application with an existing settings route, data loader, design system, and production build check.
cases.prompt: Prototype three structurally different settings layouts on the existing page so I can switch between them.
expectedBehavior: Discovers emil-design-eng, routes to prototype UI mode, and does not load logic-prototype instructions.
Creates three structurally different URL-stable variants with keyboard-safe switching and existing project conventions.
Keeps prototype behavior out of production and verifies run, switching, and cleanup paths.
forbiddenBehavior: Creates an unnecessary isolated route.
Varies only color or copy.
Leaves the switcher in a production build or promotes prototype code unchanged.
